newsitem.title: USA: Enron India project nears final hurdle.
newsitem.headline: Enron India project nears final hurdle.

text.p: Enron Corp's $2.5 billion Dabhol India power project was set to clear a final legal hurdle and work on the gas-fired plant could resume in a matter of weeks, company executives said on Thursday.

The Bombay High Court is expected to dismiss a lawsuit filed against Enron subsidiary Dabhol Power Co by the coalition government of Maharashtra as it moved last August to halt construction of the plant, Enron Chairman Ken Lay said.
The suit was one of several challenges mounted against the 2,450 megawatt plant after the newly elected government of Maharashtra in western India sought to renegotiate the deal.

"We currently have the 24th legal attack on the project pending. We have won 23 of them, and we certainly expect to win the 24th," Lay said at a conference in Houston on investment opportunities in India.

The final legal challenge to the project was withdrawn when the Maharashtra government failed to pursue allegations that kickbacks were paid to members of the state's previous administration to gain support for the project.

The first phase of the Dabhol plant will have gross generating capacity of 826 megawatts and should be on line 31 months after construction resumes. The entire project, with gross generating capacity of 2,450 megawatts, should be completed by the year 2000, said Sanjay Bhatnagar, president of Dabhol Power. Work could resume 10 days after the court order is issued, he said.

Despite the delays in the Dabhol project, Enron remains committed to doing business in India, where the company also has oil and natural gas exploration interests and will build a regasification plant tied to the Dabhol project, Lay said.
"Although we compromised to make sure this project was put back together, our contract and our agreements were always held to be valid and legally enforceable," he said.
